newsitem.title: USA: Iridium junk bonds may hinge on satellite launch.
newsitem.headline: Iridium junk bonds may hinge on satellite launch.

text.p: The pricing of a large junk bond offering from Iridium LLC scheduled for later this week will depend in part on a satellite launch scheduled for Wednesday morning, analysts said.
Iridium plans to launch five satellites into orbit on a McDonnell Douglas-manufactured Delta II rocket on Wednesday at 0904 EDT/1304 GMT.
The day after the launch, the company will attempt to raise $750 million through a 144a private placement of junk bonds via Chase Securities Inc.

"We all know if the satellites don't go up succesfully the (pricing on the) deal will widen out and it will have a harder time getting done," said David Wells, high-yield telecommunications analyst with Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Even if Wednesday's launch is successful, investors said Iridium's plans to build a worldwide wireless personal communications network were fraught with huge risks.
If this week's launch goes as planned, Iridium will have in place only 17 out of a total of 66 low-earth-orbit satellites required to complete its system.
Despite delays in a previous launch, Iridium plans to launch all of the remaining satellites by the summer of 1998 and to begin offering telecommunications services by September of 1998.

"We think their timetable is a real reach," said one investor. "It will take a lot longer to work out the kinks of this project. Meanwhile, they will have to start paying for the cost of the launches and their system."
This Thursday's junk bond offering represents one of the final components of a total of $4.4 billion in funds needed to build the telecommunications system.

According to a company spokeswoman, Iridium has already raised $2.2 billion, or 51 percent of the total cost from equity investors. An additional $223 million was raised from an initial public offering of Iridium World Communications Ltd, a unit of the parent company.
The remainder of the funds will come from $1.5 billion in bank financing. for which Iridium already has received commitments, the spokeswoman said.

Some junk bond players have expressed skepticism that Iridium's senior note offering would be able to get done at current price talk levels of around 12.0 to 12.5 percent. An additional tranche of zero coupon bonds will be offered at 125 to 150 basis points over that level.
One buy-side source said investors were facing a "Catch 22" regarding pricing on the bonds.

"There is a lot of risk in this deal and investors want to get compensated. However, if they pressure the company to pay a higher coupon, it will screw up their business plan," one buy-side trader said.
One alternative may be for Iridium to raise the equity kicker in the offering, which currently consists of warrants to purchase 1.25 to 1.5 percent of Iridium World.
"This is venture capital, and right now you are not getting paid anywhere near venture capital returns," said another investor.
Iridium is an international consortium of telecommunciations and industrial companies. U.S. owners include Motorola Inc, Lockheed Martin Corp, and Sprint Corp.
